candidates.name: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
support_spans: lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
candidates.why: The patient's lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora is a characteristic feature of Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome.

candidates.name: Meigs syndrome
support_spans: a firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm in the right lower quadrant
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of a large pelvic mass with ascites and pleural effusion is consistent with Meigs syndrome.

candidates.name: Ovarian fibroma
support_spans: a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion measuring 16.1 × 7.9 × 8.1 cm in the abdominopelvic region
candidates.why: The patient's imaging findings are consistent with an ovarian fibroma, which can cause pelvic pain and masses.

candidates.name: Malignant ovarian tumor
support_spans: Although tumor markers were normal, the imaging findings were concerning for an ovarian neoplasm
candidates.why: The patient's imaging findings and provisional diagnosis suggest a malignant ovarian tumor, which can arise from various cellular mechanisms.

candidates.name: Ovarian cystadenoma
support_spans: Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
candidates.why: The patient's ultrasound findings are consistent with an ovarian cystadenoma, which can be confirmed with imaging modalities.

candidates.name: Ovarian teratoma
support_spans: Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion
candidates.why: The patient's CT findings are consistent with an ovarian teratoma, which can be confirmed with imaging modalities.

key_evidence_spans: A 25-year-old nulliparous woman presented with a 1-month history of insidious-onset right lower abdominal pain
lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
a firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm in the right lower quadrant
Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion measuring 16.1 × 7.9 × 8.1 cm in the abdominopelvic region
Although tumor markers were normal, the imaging findings were concerning for an ovarian neoplasm
A staging laparotomy with surgical excision was planned, with a provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor in the setting of uterine fibroids and unilateral lymphedema
